The market generally expects Apple to launch a brand-new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen before the end of this month — the first Mac ever to support touch — and Apple has already laid the groundwork for touch gestures in macOS 27.2.

Apple today released macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers, which includes several new code references tied to the upcoming touch interaction features. As discovered by MacRumors' Aaron Perris, a number of built-in Apple apps have gained "gesture recognition tools":

  • Photos has gained "PXGTouchDwellGestureRecognizer"
  • Notes has gained "ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer"
  • Safari has gained "a touch sentinel recognizer"
  • Quick Look has gained a "dragTouch feature"

macOS 27.2 beta 3 has also added a new long-press animation effect to the Dock, which may be yet another clue hinting at the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro:

Apple has already made a series of changes in macOS 27 to prepare for touchscreen support, including the first-ever addition of a pull-to-refresh feature. macOS 27 has also added touch input support to Sidecar, the feature that lets you use an iPad as a secondary display for your Mac.

Bloomberg has previously reported that Apple is optimising macOS for the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro. For example, when tapping buttons or controls, macOS will dynamically display the relevant touch options; likewise, when tapping the menu bar, controls will automatically enlarge for easier touch operation.

On top of the touchscreen, the new MacBook Pro is reported to feature an OLED display and be "significantly lighter" than current models.

The outside world expects Apple to unveil this new MacBook Pro (or should it be called the MacBook Ultra?) before the end of this month, though Bloomberg cautions that a delay to November is possible.
